data.subject: cmd:complete.force:B95-false-limit:unit_tests
data.text:
Approve gated command 'complete.force' for agent resume-b95?
  command : ddflow complete <id> --approval request|ID
  item    : B95-false-limit    target: unit_tests
  acts on : the item and its unmet completion conditions (never a failed review gate)
  digest  : 521aa6bae5410059  (the state is read again when the agent runs it)
  needs   : tier T2, assurance level L1 or stronger; 1 use(s)
  agent's reason (untrusted, not part of the approval): ""
  approved by standing rule: complete_unavailable

overridden: required gate(s) not passed: unit_tests (current outcome: unit_tests=partial); unit_tests is partial and baseline-red but was not accepted automatically (failing test file(s) the item changed or reaches: tests/test_architecture_counters.py, tests/test_architecture_guards.py, tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py, tests/test_digest_sites.py, tests/test_kind_pipeline.py, tests/test_module_splits.py, tests/test_na_evidence_record.py, tests/test_stale_after_merge.py). Do NOT request an approval: fix what it names, then re-run it (CLI `ddflow gate run B95-false-limit unit_tests`, MCP ddflow_gate action=run id=B95-false-limit gate=unit_tests). Only a person, who runs `ddflow approve B95-false-limit unit_tests`, accepts it otherwise

data.summary: `ddflow complete B95-false-limit --model claude-opus-5-5`, with no --force and no --approval, filed Q814c2b642e and policy:complete_unavailable answered it, so the item completed forced over unit_tests=partial (item.completed forced=true, 2026-11-05T10:54:24). The same state had just been reported by `ddflow recover` as "refused for now", and gate_accept.next_step says "Do NOT request an approval ... Only a person, who runs `ddflow approve`, accepts it otherwise". _auto_complete_unavailable (api/lifecycle/complete/approval.py) fires for any partial, including one auto_decision has just declined because its failing tests are in the item's reach, so the person-only rule has no effect once the author model is known; the unknown model was the only thing keeping it refused. The success reply carries forced=true but no warning that an override was filed and spent, and an agent cannot ask for a refusal-only run. Expected: a measured baseline-red partial with baseline.auto.accepted=false is not answered by complete_unavailable, or recover and next_step state plainly that the next complete will force. Also wanted: a dry-run of complete.
data.title: A plain complete self-approves complete.force over a baseline-red partial that ddflow says only a person accepts

data.body:

The success reply carries forced=true but no warning that an override was filed and spent, and an agent cannot ask for a refusal-only run. Expected: a measured baseline-red partial with baseline.auto.accepted=false is not answered by complete_unavailable, or recover and next_step state plainly that the next complete will force. data.summary: gate_accept.next_step tells an agent to `ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests`. For a merged item whose base moved on, item_tree returns None from the primary and from a clean worktree at merged_sha (probed read-only on B95-false-limit: _at_merged_tree False on the primary, True at 1889d59ed, item_tree (None, '') in both), so _no_tree_reason keeps only a prior `passed` and record_measured writes `unavailable` over the partial. That erases evidence baseline.red, the only thing `ddflow approve` can accept (gate_accept.refusal), and unavailable then feeds complete_unavailable. No re-run can settle such a partial, so the advice is wrong and destructive. The same message offers `gate record --outcome passed` to a gate that did not pass. Expected: keep a measured partial as a passed one is kept, and say that only a person can settle it. Not run on the real item; read-only probe plus code reading (api/gates/_tree.py, _run.py).
data.title: Re-running a merged item's baseline-red partial as advised records unavailable over the measurement
